name: get_postgres_metrics
description: Returns bucketed time-series metrics for a Postgres service over a time window (CPU, memory, disk, network, connections, cache hit ratio, throughput, transactions, wait events, lock waits, and more). Wait metrics are active_sessions_by_wait (one series per wait event, such as Lock:relation, or None when a session is not waiting), lock_wait_time (p50, p95, and Max series, in seconds), and blocked_sessions. Each metric has a key, name, unit, description, and one series per label dimension, where each series is a list of (timestamp, value) data points. Timestamps are Unix seconds at the bucket start. Provide fromDate and toDate to bound the window; omit bucketSizeSeconds to let the server pick a bucket granularity for the window. Use this to chart or analyze how a service behaved over time.

bucketSizeSeconds.description: Width of each time bucket in seconds. Omit to let the server pick a granularity that suits the window; larger buckets return fewer data points.

fromDate.description: Inclusive start of the time window. Pass a UTC timestamp with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-06-08T00:00:00.000Z.

organizationId.description: Organization that owns the Postgres service. Use the id of an organization returned by get_organizations.

serviceId.description: Managed Postgres service to read metrics for. Use the id of a postgres-type service returned by get_services_list.

toDate.description: Exclusive end of the time window. Pass a UTC timestamp with millisecond precision, e.g. 2026-06-09T00:00:00.000Z.
